Builddrone 0.4.1 is a security release. It extends symlink protections to
additional modules that read or publish files, and hardens the documentation
deployment workflow against shell injection.

**Documentation:** https://nepitwin.github.io/Builddrone/latest/

---

## Security fixes

### Filesystem copy symlink handling

`filesystem.copy` no longer materializes symlink targets as regular files when
copying a source tree. Folder walks use `followlinks=False`, and symlinked files
are detected with `Path.is_symlink()` and skipped with a warning.

This prevents contributor-planted symlinks from bypassing the archiver symlink
guard and leaking host file contents into later publish steps.

### AppVeyor test upload symlink rejection

`appveyor.upload.tests` now rejects symlinked results files in `_resolve_source`
before `read_bytes()` can follow them to host paths. Uploads fail with a clear
error instead of sending symlink target contents to AppVeyor.

### Twine upload symlink rejection

`twine.upload` now rejects symlink matches in `_resolve_glob` before paths are
passed to `twine upload`. A contributor-planted symlink under a glob such as
`dist/*` can no longer cause host file bytes to be published to the configured
package index.

### Documentation workflow injection hardening

The `docs.yml` workflow no longer interpolates `${{ inputs.version }}` directly
into bash script text. Release versions are passed through environment variables,
validated against a semver-style pattern, and quoted when passed to `mike deploy`.

This prevents remote code execution via crafted `workflow_dispatch` input when
the workflow runs with `contents: write`.
